detailed_findings.finding: The sign argument for (a-b)(n-a-b) is complete: a-b<0 and a+b<2b<=n implies n-a-b>0.

reason: The proof correctly defines degree on nonzero rational functions, computes deg_q([n choose a]_q) by decomposing the Gaussian binomial into factors of degree n-a, and then derives deg_q(([n choose a]_q)/([n choose b]_q)) = (a-b)(n-a-b) < 0 under 0 <= a < b <= n/2. Since the quotient is shown nonzero, negative degree excludes membership in Q[q]. The argument matches the lemma sketch and its stated role after symmetry reduction.
